summary: Session anchoring split under sudden traffic surge causes fallback to legacy variant
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a subset of live requests suddenly receiving responses from legacy model variant during an ongoing canary. Impact: ~8% of tenant requests returned older model outputs for ~11 minutes, causing quality regressions and a rollback of a critical feature. Environment: dedicated prod us-west; tenant on reserved pool. Observed behavior: Session anchoring tokens were duplicated across two edge shards after an edge prewarm burst; orchestrator commit lag plus cookie rotation caused cohort assignment to split and route some traffic to the fallback/legacy variant despite model pin for the tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reproduce on prod-like cluster with dedicated tenant and weighted canary (10% traffic to v2, 90% to v1)
2) Simulate sudden traffic surge on edge (10x short burst) while rotating session cookies every 60s
3) Observe edge-proxy logs for duplicate session tokens and orchestrator commit latency spikes
4) Confirm some requests are routed to v1 despite tenant pin to v2 using routing trace headers
logs: edge-proxy: WARN duplicate-session-token detected shard-A <-> shard-B at 2026-03-13T14:22:08Z
orchestrator: INFO commit-delay=1234ms snapshot-version=15892 during weight-change 2026-03-13T14:22:09Z
serving-runtime: ERROR model-selection fallback-to=redwood/gptx-13b-v1 reason=affinity-mismatch request_id=abc123
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Edge token mirror + cookie rotation TTL race caused two different edge shards to present conflicting affinity metadata to the orchestrator, leading to inconsistent routing decisions.
Found: Orchestrator commit path slowed by database leader election on config-store around 14:22 UTC; commit-delay correlated with measured window of user-impact.

Found: Edge prewarm path duplicates session-cookie header when upstream returns 307 prewarm redirect under high concurrent connections. This creates transient duplicate tokens with different shard-scoped signatures.

Telemetry: Trace spans show some requests carrying header X-Session-Anchored: shard-A while control plane snapshot indicated shard-B affinity; resulting routing hit fallback policy that preferred stable legacy variant when affinity cannot be reconciled.
Customer impact: Streamly AI reported increased hallucination rate for affected requests; they triggered rollback of canary for business-critical cohort.
comments: Ava Patel (Support): Initial triage complete. We see ~11-minute window where 6-10% of tenant traffic hit legacy model. Collecting full traces and config-store timeline.
Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced duplicate session-cookie behavior in staging by simulating prewarm redirects. Filed PR to edge-proxy to dedupe cookies on redirect path. See PR linked.
Customer (Streamly AI - Emily Zhang): Confirmed rollback executed at 14:34 UTC. We need assurance this won't recur during next rollout; please prioritize mitigation.

Diego Morales (SRE): Mitigations planned: 1) Hotfix to dedupe session headers on redirect, 2) Orchestrator config-store leader failover tuning to keep commit-delay <200ms under burst, 3) Add preflight check in rollout controller to validate session-affinity consistency before raising weights.
Ava Patel (Support): Scheduled follow-up call with customer for 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC to review RCA and mitigation timeline.
resolution: Workaround applied: Increased canary safety gate to delay weight shifts while edge-snapshot in-progress; this prevented additional impact during incident window.

Fixes deployed: edge-proxy hotfix v1.12.3 to dedupe session cookies on redirect (deployed 2026-03-13 19:20 UTC), orchestrator config-store tuning commit pushed (PR merged), rollout-controller preflight added (feature flag off by default).

Post-incident actions: Runbook updated with explicit prewarm redirect handling steps, add synthetic test that simulates simultaneous cookie rotation + prewarm, and schedule regression test in next canary runbook (owner: Diego Morales).
Status: Monitoring. Customer has asked for written RCA and compensatory credits; CS/Finance loop opened (CS owner: Ava Patel).
